Topics · One God, one message

Isn't my faith just where I happened to be born?

Where a belief comes from explains why you hold it, not if it is true. The Quran says weigh, do not inherit.

Part 1 of 4

﴿بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ٢٢ وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِى قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدْنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ٢٣ قَـٰلَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُم بِأَهْدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمْ عَلَيْهِ ءَابَآءَكُمْ ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِۦ كَـٰفِرُونَ٢٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

Rather, they say, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are in their footsteps [rightly] guided." And similarly, We did not send before you any warner into a city except that its affluent said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are, in their footsteps, following." [Each warner] said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that [religion] upon which you found your fathers?" They said, "Indeed we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."

Quran · Az-Zukhruf 43:22-24

Translation

Don’t you be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying: Yahweh of Armies says, ‘Return now from your evil ways and from your evil doings;’ but they didn’t hear nor listen to me, says Yahweh.

Original · Hebrew

אַל־תִּהְי֣וּ כַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרְאֽוּ־אֲלֵיהֶם֩ הַנְּבִיאִ֨ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת שׁ֤וּבוּ נָא֙ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֣ם הָרָעִ֔ים וּמַֽעֲלְלֵיכֶ֖ם הָֽרָעִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֛וּ וְלֹֽא־הִקְשִׁ֥יבוּ אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

Zechariah · 1:4

World English Bible

The objection is old and weighty. Most people hold the beliefs of the place they grew up in, and the same person born elsewhere would likely believe something else. The verse records people giving this very reason for their faith: we found our elders on a way, and we follow their footsteps. The reply it records is a question: what if what I bring is better guidance than your elders held? It does not deny the objection. It asks you to weigh what is offered against what you received.

A question for you

If you had been born elsewhere, would your own view have changed?

If you sayProbably, and that applies to my doubts too
ThenThen the objection cuts evenly. It applies to whatever you hold, including doubt, and including the opinion that nothing can be known.
If you sayMine came from my own thinking, not where I was born
ThenPerhaps. It is worth asking where the questions you asked came from, and which ones you never thought to ask. Even our own thinking begins somewhere.
If you sayPartly, and I cannot tell how much
ThenAn honest answer, and the right size for the claim. The next parts ask what to do with it.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not pursue[745] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

Translator's notes

[745] i.e., do not assume and do not say.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

Original · Ancient Greek

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:36-37

World English Bible

Here is the step that matters. How a belief reached you tells you why you hold it. It does not tell you whether it is true. A person raised among doctors learns medicine from them, and the medicine can still be sound or unsound. If origin decided truth, the same logic would sink the belief that origin decides truth. The verse sets the fair standard instead: do not pursue what you have no knowledge of, and use your hearing, sight and heart yourself, since each will be asked.

A question for you

Which of your beliefs did you examine, and which did you only receive?

If you sayMostly examined
ThenThen you can say where you looked. The verse's standard is one you can show your work on, so it helps to be able to name where the examining happened.
If you sayMostly received
ThenThat is where nearly everyone begins. What matters to the verse is what you do with it next: whether you look.
If you sayA mix, and I cannot tell which is which
ThenThat is the usual state, and the beginning of an honest list. Pick one belief and walk it back to where it came from.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَن يَدْخُلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَن كَانَ هُودًا أَوْ نَصَـٰرَىٰ ۗ تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ ۗ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:111

Translation

Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, are these.’

Original · Hebrew

אַל־תִּבְטְח֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖קֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃

Jeremiah · 7:4

World English Bible

﴿لَّيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَآ أَمَانِىِّ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ ۗ مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوٓءًا يُجْزَ بِهِۦ وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

It [i.e., Paradise] is not [obtained] by your wishful thinking nor by that of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allāh a protector or a helper.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:123

Translation

“I, Yahweh, search the mind. I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”

Original · Hebrew

אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה חֹקֵ֥ר לֵ֖ב בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת וְלָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כִּפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃

Jeremiah · 17:10

World English Bible

Many groups say: we are the ones. The verse hears one group claim paradise for itself alone, calls that wishful thinking, and answers: bring your evidence if you are truthful. Another verse, aimed at the book's own followers, puts the same standard on them: it is not by your wishes, nor by the wishes of the others. So the standard favours neither side. It is the same for those born inside a tradition and those born outside.

A question for you

What would count as proof for you?

If you sayA reason I can follow step by step
ThenThen you are asking for an argument, and the book gives some. Later steps in this series lay them out in order.
If you sayA test I can run myself
ThenThen you are asking for something the book itself offers in places: a test to try, not a belief to adopt. A later question in this series is about that.
If you saySomething I would have to see
ThenReasonable. It helps to decide in advance what seeing would look like, so you would recognise it when it came.
If you sayI do not know yet
ThenAn honest place to be. Writing down a first guess, however rough, makes it easier to notice when the answer arrives.

Part 4 of 4

﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍ ۖ أَن تَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا۟ ۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍ ۚ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَّكُم بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I only advise you of one [thing] - that you stand for Allāh, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.

Quran · Saba 34:46

How can you examine a belief that arrived with your family? The verse offers a method so simple it is easy to miss: stand up, alone or with one other person, and then think. Not in a crowd, because a crowd tends to think like a crowd. Take one belief. Sit with it by yourself or with someone you trust. Ask what you would say if you were asked to explain it to a stranger who had no reason to be polite.

A question for you

Who would you choose to think it through with?

If you saySomeone who agrees with me
ThenA gentle way to begin, and a safe one. The verse's one other person works best if they are willing to ask honest questions, not only to agree.
If you saySomeone who does not
ThenA brave choice and a useful one, if they are kind. Disagreement only helps if both of you are curious.
If you sayNobody; alone
ThenThat is the other half of the method: singly. Take a notebook, and write the strongest objection to your own view.

The same in the other books

Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue. In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 360-361

Max Müller, 1881

Translation

He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
